what_it_does: This paper evaluates using large language models (LLMs) for HPC job scheduling. The scheduler balances multiple competing goals: minimizing total completion time, reducing wait time, maximizing resource utilization, and ensuring fairness. It uses the ReAct framework where the LLM reasons through scheduling decisions, maintains a scratchpad of history, receives natural-language feedback on its choices, and has a module to ensure constraints are met. The evaluation compares Claude and OpenAI models against traditional scheduling algorithms.
